title: UK labour market overview — earnings, unemployment and vacancies (ONS, 07:00 London / 02:00 ET), the FIRST release whose average-weekly-earnings window is wholly after the 2026-10-28 Autumn Budget
source: EST: gov.uk/government/statistics/announcements/uk-labour-market-march-2027, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200) — the statutory pre-announcement register reads 'UK Labour Market: March 2027', '16 March 2027 at 7:00am', status 'Confirmed', announcement page published 30 June 2026, covering employment, unemployment, inactivity, earnings and vacancies. Filed estimate per this lane's no-self-confirm limit and because market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no slot for the UK Office for National Statistics. Discovered in the never-assessed initial research of uk-labour-market-2027-01-19, 2026-09-09
notes: PROPOSED BY THE uk-labour-market-2027-01-19 LANE, 2026-09-09, and it is filed BECAUSE IT IS THE ANSWER THIS CHAIN HAS TWICE GOT WRONG. Four documents in the UK labour chain have now reasoned about which release first carries an average-weekly-earnings window wholly after the 2026-10-28 Autumn Budget. The uk-labour-market-2026-11-17 lane refuted the claim for its own print; the uk-labour-market-2026-12-15 lane refuted it again for its own; and BOTH the 12-15 ledger's leg 8 and the proposal that created uk-labour-market-2027-01-19 then named 'the FEBRUARY 2027 release' as the first that qualifies. THE ARITHMETIC SAYS MARCH, on the chain's own rule. That rule — the headline AWE/LFS window is the three months ending TWO months before the release month — is reconfirmed across four bulletins, most recently firsthand from the 18 August 2026 bulletin (Apr-Jun AWE/LFS, May-Jul vacancies, Jul payroll flash), and its cleanest anchor is the release that shares this one's month: the 19 March 2026 bulletin carried Nov 2025-Jan 2026. So the February 2027 release carries OCT-DEC 2026, of which 27 of October's 31 days precede Budget day, and THIS release carries NOV 2026-JAN 2027 — the first window with no pre-Budget day in it. TWO HONEST QUALIFICATIONS, both stated so the entry cannot be over-read. First, 'wholly post-Budget' is a statement about the reference window, NOT a prediction that a Budget wage effect appears in it: UK employer-cost measures conventionally take effect the following April (Autumn Budget 2024-10-30 raised secondary Class 1 NICs from 13.8% to 15% effective April 2025 — the uk-labour-market-2026-11-17 lane's finding, carried by reference), so the first plausible venue for a measured response remains the April 2027 data published in June 2027. Second, this release lands D-2 to the 2027-03-18 MPC round (bankofengland.co.uk/monetary-policy/upcoming-mpc-dates, fetched today: 'Thursday 18 March', provisional, summary and minutes only), proposed in the same PR — the same D-2 non-Report geometry the 12-15 lane settled from the March and June 2026 precedents. TIERED LOW on the same argued grounds as every sibling: symbols [], no UK-listed symbol tracked, no rates- or sterling-keyed house playbook. Estimate widens caution only; it licenses no date-keyed action.
